tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Check whether domain names are registered, asking each TLD's registry directly (RDAP). Returns registered, available, likely_available (no registry lookup service, but no DNS records either) or unknown, plus the registrar and dates for taken names and the cheapest prices for open ones. Up to 20 name

tools.name: compare_prices
tools.description: Every tracked registrar's price for one TLD, in US dollars per year, refreshed daily from 40+ registrars. Sorted by 3-year cost (first year plus two renewals) by default, because a cheap first year often hides an expensive renewal. Each offer links to where to buy.

tools.name: suggest_names
tools.description: Turn a few keywords into domain name candidates (the words joined, with common prefixes and suffixes, across several TLDs), check each with its registry, and return the available ones with prices. For your own name ideas, use check_availability.

tools.name: tld_info
tools.description: Who runs a TLD, its type (generic, country-code, ...), when it was delegated, its registry's website and lookup servers (from IANA), and its cheapest first-year, renewal and 3-year prices.

tools.name: price_history
tools.description: Every recorded price change for one TLD, oldest first, from GoMain's daily archive. A registrar's first entry is its price when the archive began (or when it started selling the TLD); later entries are changes. Prices are per year, in US dollars unless `currency` says otherwise.

tools.name: check_name
tools.description: Is a project name usable everywhere it'll be needed? Checks the domain across TLDs (with prices), GitHub, npm, PyPI and crates.io, and gives links for trademark and social-handle checks that can't be automated.

tools.name: dns_setup
tools.description: The exact DNS records to add so a domain serves a website (Vercel, Netlify, GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages) and receives email (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Fastmail, Zoho, Proton), plus a starting DMARC policy. Checks live DNS to show which records are already in place and warns about clashes s

tools.name: appraise_domain
tools.description: A rough value range for a domain, from its length, how easy it is to say, its TLD, its age and how many popular TLDs have the same name registered. Use it to set a realistic budget before trying to buy a taken name. Not a comparable-sales appraisal.

tools.description: Ask GoMain's brokerage to acquire a domain someone else owns. GoMain researches it, approaches the owner without naming the buyer, negotiates within the budget (which the owner never sees), and closes through Escrow.com. tools.description: Search domains their owners have listed for sale with GoMain (each owner proved control of the name). Returns asking prices where set; make_offer buys or negotiates.

tools.description: Offer to buy a domain listed with GoMain. tools.name: watch_domain
tools.description: GoMain checks a domain daily and emails when it drops (or is about to), changes hands, or is listed for sale. Returns a watch id and status key for broker_status.

tools.name: broker_status
tools.description: The status and history of a brokerage deal (id d_…) or a watch (id w_…), given the id and status key returned when it was created.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_acquisition" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Ask GoMain's brokerage to acquire a domain someone else owns. GoMain researches it, approaches the owner without naming the buyer, negotiates within the budget …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_domain_for_sale · Private data: check_availability, dns_setup, list_domain_for_sale · Public sink: dns_setup, request_acquisition, make_offer, list_domain_for_sale · Destructive: acquisition_report.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_domain_for_sale · Private data: check_availability, dns_setup, list_domain_for_sale · Public sink: dns_setup, request_acquisition, make_offer, list_domain_for_sale · Destructive: acquisition_report

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
